display_name: Send peer message by role name
description: Resolve a durable fleet role at send time, persist the role envelope, and attempt delivery to the current holder without caching an ephemeral instance id. An offline resolved holder returns queued_for_replay; a vacant role fails before persistence. The result also reports the holder's managed-drive disposition: not_managed means completed state reads found no managed row, ineligible_state means the holder's row is outside the driveable lifecycle states, driver_unavailable means the state or driver channel could not be resolved, and driver_scheduled means an inbox notice was queued on the bounded delivery-drive executor without the send waiting for it; that drive's finished driver_sent or driver_error is logged against the message_id. driver_queue_full means the bounded drive queue was at its cap, so no notice was queued; the message itself is still durable. A queued drive re-checks the recipient's lifecycle before touching its pane, so a recipient parked or retired meanwhile logs ineligible_state instead of driver_sent. Neither proves a model turn or message consumption.
embedding_description: Route a durable message to the current holder of a named fleet role, including reconnect-safe queued_for_replay behavior and managed-drive diagnosis. Search for role dispatch outcomes not_managed, ineligible_state, driver_unavailable, driver_scheduled, and driver_queue_full; a scheduled drive is a queued notice rather than recipient uptake.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Peer message delivered by role name
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Returns thread_id, message_id, delivery, the role name's resolved holder tuple, and drive_on_delivery. delivery may be queued_notification, queued_wake, queued_watcher, or queued_for_replay and describes persistence/routing rather than model uptake. drive_on_delivery is not_managed (completed lookup found no row), ineligible_state (managed lifecycle refuses a drive), driver_unavailable (lookup or channel unavailable), driver_scheduled (notice queued on the delivery-drive executor; its driver_sent or driver_error is logged against message_id), or driver_queue_full (drive queue at its cap; no notice queued). driver_scheduled does not prove a model turn or inbox consumption.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Name the role and the exact resolved_session_label, then surface both delivery and drive_on_delivery without converting either into a consumption claim. Treat queued_for_replay as durable but not live delivery. Treat not_managed and ineligible_state as distinct routing facts, driver_unavailable as an unsuccessful drive attempt, and driver_scheduled solely as a queued driver notice pending independent turn evidence.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Resolves a durable role binding at act time, persists to the role thread, delivery-attempts the current holder, and separately reports the managed driver outcome.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: peer_role_vacant means no holder exists and nothing was persisted; peer_role_malformed means the binding lacks an instance id; bridge.not_running and state_service_unavailable identify missing infrastructure. An offline holder is a queued_for_replay result. not_managed, ineligible_state, driver_unavailable, driver_scheduled, and driver_queue_full are drive_on_delivery result values; none alone proves consumption.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Repair vacant or malformed role ownership from the intended holder with peer_claim_role, then route by name again so resolution occurs fresh. When a persisted result reports not_managed, ineligible_state, or driver_unavailable, or a scheduled drive logs driver_error, verify holder lineage and choose a supported recovery channel. Even after a drive is scheduled or sent, require a causal reply or equivalent model-turn evidence before declaring uptake.
